### Added
- **Self-management through the bundled Flux, on by default** (roadmap#4348, PRD Q5/Q5b): where the chart brings the engine, the engine also holds the chart. `gitops.self.enabled` (`auto` | `true` | `false`, default `auto` = follows `components.flux.enabled`; `true` with the engine off fails the render) renders the release's own `OCIRepository` + `HelmRelease` (`templates/self/release.yaml`, both named after the release, in the release namespace, run as `agent-platform-flux` — `gitops.serviceAccountName` overrides it — `chartRef` to the `OCIRepository`, `releaseName`/`targetNamespace` the release's, `install`/`upgrade.disableWait`, values from Secret `agent-platform-values` key `values.yaml` with `optional: false`). The `OCIRepository` follows `<gitops.self.repository>/agent-platform` (default `oci://gsoci.azurecr.io/charts/giantswarm`; `gitops.self.insecure` for a plain-HTTP lab registry) at `>=<installed version> <next major>.0.0`, derived from the running chart at render time (`gitops.self.versionRange` overrides; an offline `helm template` derives it from the placeholder `Chart.yaml` version), on `gitops.self.interval` (default `10m`). The bundled helm-controller adopts the CLI-installed release with one extra revision and rolls the chart forward inside its major without a `helm upgrade`. Measured on kind: install `--wait` 87 s, adoption in the second the release went `deployed`, a pushed version applied 47 s after the push with the new chart default in effect and the user's values intact, a rewritten values Secret applied within 20 s, uninstall `--wait` with the self `HelmRelease` present in under a minute, the upgrade from an engine-on 3.18.0 into this version adopted with the bracket held.
- **The install-time bracket**: the self `HelmRelease` is rendered `suspend: true` on `helm install` and whenever it does not exist yet (a guarded `lookup` — the upgrade of an engine-on installation into this version), never on a controller-driven upgrade; the post-install/post-upgrade hook `<release>-self-values` (weight 0) writes the **user-supplied** values of the revision in flight (`helm get values`, never the merged tree) into Secret `agent-platform-values`, labelled `reconcile.fluxcd.io/watch=Enabled`, by server-side apply, and — only while the `HelmRelease` is suspended — starts the detached Job `<release>-self-resume`, which polls `helm status` and resumes the `HelmRelease` once the release is `deployed` (or `failed`); still pending after 300 s it exits 1 *without* resuming. Neither is a chart object Helm's kstatus `--wait` would wait on. `helm template` renders `suspend: true`.
- **The Helm CLI is day-0 only — a `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy`** (`templates/self/policy.yaml`: `<release>-self-managed-<namespace>` + a binding of the same name scoped to the release namespace, `failurePolicy: Fail`) on the CREATE of Secrets of type `helm.sh/release.v1` labelled `name=<release>`: admitted for `system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:agent-platform-flux` (the identity the bundled helm-controller impersonates) or while the namespace carries `agent-platform.giantswarm.io/helm-cli=allow`. `helm upgrade` and `helm rollback` fail in about a second with the reason in Helm's own error output (the message names Secret `agent-platform-values` and the hand-back) and write no revision; UPDATE/DELETE pass, so does `helm uninstall`. Needs Kubernetes ≥ 1.30: the render refuses an older cluster while self-management is on. A render guard also refuses the annotation together with self-management on (two writers on one release). The guard-Job alternative (a pre-upgrade hook reading the pending storage Secret's `managedFields` manager) stays documented in UPGRADE.md as the fallback should the policy ever be ruled out.
- **The hand-back / escape hatch**: `kubectl annotate namespace <ns> agent-platform.giantswarm.io/helm-cli=allow`, then `helm upgrade … --set gitops.self.enabled=false --force-conflicts` (once; helm-controller co-owns the fields) hands the release back to the CLI without an uninstall — the new pre-upgrade hooks suspend the self `HelmRelease` before Helm deletes it, so helm-controller drops its finalizer; the value stays in the values file (README "Self-management").
- **Teardown extended** (`templates/hooks/self.yaml`, rendered whenever the engine is on): weight -6 `<release>-self-stop-resumer` (one plain `kubectl delete` of the resumer Job, `--ignore-not-found`) and weight -5 `<release>-self-suspend` (suspends the self `HelmRelease` if present, removes the hook-written values Secret by its labels) at `pre-delete` — and at `pre-upgrade` too while self-management is off (the hand-back and lab renders). They run as the new namespaced identity `<release>-self` (ServiceAccount + Role + RoleBinding, `templates/self/rbac.yaml`, regular objects: the detached resumer runs after a hook-managed account is gone), as do the values hook and the resumer. `gitops.hooks.helmImage` (`docker.io/alpine/k8s:1.36.4` — kubectl, helm, jq, a shell; Renovate-tracked like `gitops.hooks.image`) runs the hooks that need helm or have to tolerate a missing object; `templates/hooks/_job.tpl` takes `script`, `image` and `serviceAccountName`.
- **Lab shape**: `gitops.self.enabled: false` renders none of it (no self objects, no values hook, no policy) but the -6/-5 hooks and their identity; `tests/test-values.yaml` sets it — the ATS installs an unreleased chart, which a self `HelmRelease` would replace with the published one — and `tests/ats/test_smoke.py` asserts the lab shape on the cluster. `make verify-self` (`tests/verify-self.py`, in CI with Helm 3.17.3) asserts the three shapes, the guards and the knobs; `make verify-engine` renders its engine-on shape with self-management off. **No installation needs to act**: the fleet (engine off) renders byte-identically; an engine-on CLI installation becomes self-managed on its next `helm upgrade` — see UPGRADE.md.
